parts.label: wave-efficiency
parts.display_text: A sea-wave generator converts wave energy to electricity. Explain why the useful electrical power is less than the power carried by the waves.

answer.text: Some wave energy passes the device or is reflected; friction, turbulence and electrical resistance also transfer energy to the surroundings. The conversion efficiency is therefore below 100%.

source.title: IB Physics HL Paper-2 specimen markscheme

parts.label: coal-climate
parts.display_text: Explain one effect of coal-fired electricity generation on the greenhouse effect.

answer.text: Burning coal releases CO₂. Greater atmospheric CO₂ increases absorption and re-emission of outgoing infrared radiation, strengthening the greenhouse effect.

parts.label: fission-resources
parts.display_text: State one resource limitation and one environmental concern associated with electricity from uranium fission.

answer.text: Uranium fuel is a finite mined resource. Radioactive waste requires isolation and management over long periods; accidental releases are another environmental concern.

answer.text: Official answer D; editorial worked explanation: The distance between extremes is b, so amplitude A=b/2. Halfway from equilibrium to an extreme means |x|=A/2=b/4. For SHM, v=ω√(A²−x²), with ω=2πf. Hence v=2πf√(b²/4−b²/16)=2πf(b√3/4)=(√3/2)πfb, option D.

answer.text:
Official answer D checked; editorial worked explanation:

For SHM, a = -omega^2 x. Acceleration is always opposite in sign to displacement, so their sinusoidal variations differ by pi radians. Therefore D.

sup-064316255265a882-0HL1q11:whole.hint: Compare the acceleration with displacement from equilibrium, including its direction.
notes: Simple harmonic motion satisfies a = −ω²x: acceleration is proportional to displacement and points towards equilibrium. ω = 2πf = 2π/T.
Displacement is measured from equilibrium, not necessarily from the spring’s natural length. At equilibrium acceleration is zero while speed is greatest.

notes: For SHM, v² = ω²(A² − x²), and total energy is ½mω²A². The kinetic energy depends on how far the oscillator is from equilibrium.
At a turning point speed is zero; at equilibrium its magnitude is ωA. Doubling amplitude changes total energy by a factor of four, not two.

sup-f78f5db8b521f4d0-w10:d.ii.hint: Follow what happens to the original heavy nucleus and to the particles that can trigger the next event.
notes: In fission, a heavy nucleus splits into lighter fragments, usually releasing neutrons and energy. The products have greater total binding energy.
Neutrons can enter a nucleus without electrostatic repulsion. Distinguish initiating a fission event from sustaining a chain reaction.

sup-f78f5db8b521f4d0-w10:d.iii.hint: Match each reactor component to the quantity it changes: neutron speed, neutron number, or heat transfer.
notes: A moderator slows neutrons; control rods absorb neutrons; coolant removes thermal energy. These are distinct functions.
A steady chain reaction requires, on average, one subsequent fission per fission event. Critical mass depends on neutron production, absorption and escape, including the material’s geometry.

sup-f78f5db8b521f4d0-w10:d.iv.hint: Consider both the repulsion between nuclei and the chance of collisions while the fuel is confined.
notes: Fusion combines light nuclei into more tightly bound products. High temperature helps nuclei approach, high density increases collision rates, and confinement time allows reactions to occur.
Energy release comes from the mass difference or increase in total binding energy. High temperature is a condition for fusion; it is not the source of the released nuclear energy.
